title: Quran Knowledge
description: General User → Mid. Familiar Quran facts, broader basics and short everyday applications focused on messages of well-known passages, responsible reading and simple connections. All questions are Mid level; specialist terminology, obscure trivia and reference-number memorization are excluded.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires more understanding and simple connections than Beginner, without specialist study. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Everyday scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: What command appears at the start of the first Quranic revelation?

options.text: Read or recite in the name of your Lord
Travel to another country immediately
Count the stars before speaking
Write a history of every nation

questions.explanation: The first revealed passage begins with reading or reciting in the name of the Creator.

questions.question: How was the Quran conveyed to the Prophet over his mission?

options.text: As a book he composed after his mission
In portions, over time
Only through one public speech
Through later teachers after his death

questions.explanation: The Quran describes its revelation in stages so it could be recited to people gradually.

questions.question: What wisdom for gradual revelation is specifically mentioned in the Quran?

options.text: Keeping guidance unavailable to people
Allowing people to invent missing verses
Strengthening the Prophet's heart
Making revelation depend on popularity

questions.explanation: The Quran explains that revelation in stages strengthened the Prophet's heart.

questions.question: What does the description Al-Furqan emphasize about the Quran?

options.text: It is only a collection of travel accounts
It is useful only for counting dates
It gives every reader personal knowledge of the future
It distinguishes truth from falsehood

questions.explanation: Al-Furqan describes revelation as a criterion or decisive standard.

questions.question: Which message is central to Ayat al-Kursi?

options.text: Allah's perfect life, knowledge and authority
Human independence from Allah
The appointment of a new prophet
A detailed account of a battle

questions.explanation: Ayat al-Kursi describes Allah's greatness and His sustaining authority over creation.

questions.question: What guidance do worshippers request in Al-Fatihah?

options.text: A promise of wealth without responsibility
Guidance to the straight path
Knowledge of every person's future
Freedom from all duties

questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah combines worship and seeking help with a request for right guidance.

questions.question: From what does Surah An-Nas teach people to seek Allah's protection?

options.text: Every kind of useful advice
All human contact
The evil of whispering that draws people toward wrong
Learning about one's responsibilities

questions.explanation: The surah seeks refuge in Allah from the whisperer, including whispering from jinn and humans.

questions.question: Which statement agrees with Surah Al-Ikhlas?

options.text: Allah was born before creation
Allah has an equal who shares His divinity
Allah depends on His creatures
Allah has neither parent nor offspring

questions.explanation: The surah declares Allah's oneness and uniqueness, including that He is not born and has no offspring.

questions.question: Which four qualities are joined in Surah Al-Asr?

options.text: Faith, good deeds, encouraging truth and encouraging patience
Wealth, fame, strength and family rank
Travel, trade, victory and public praise
Silence, isolation, possessions and appearance

questions.explanation: Al-Asr links avoiding loss with faith, righteous action and mutual encouragement in truth and patience.

questions.question: Besides neglecting those in need, what behavior does Al-Maun criticize?

options.text: Offering practical assistance
Showing off and withholding small acts of help
Sincere prayer
Kindness toward orphans

questions.explanation: The surah connects concern for others with sincere worship and warns against refusing small kindnesses.

questions.question: Which blessings are recalled as reasons to worship the Lord of the House in Surah Quraysh?

options.text: A guarantee that no one will ever face hardship
Unlimited authority over other peoples
Food against hunger and safety against fear
Permission to ignore every duty

questions.explanation: Surah Quraysh calls attention to Allah's provision of food and security.

questions.question: What fundamental warning does Luqman give his son?

options.text: Never ask anyone a question
Judge people only by wealth
Treat family status as a replacement for faith
Do not associate partners with Allah

questions.explanation: Luqman's advice begins by warning against shirk, described as a great wrong.

questions.question: How does the Quran describe the young people of the Cave?

options.text: Young believers whose guidance Allah increased
People rewarded for denying Allah
Rulers seeking fame through cruelty
People who knew every future event

questions.explanation: Their story includes faith in Allah and His granting them increased guidance.

questions.question: What response does Yusuf give his brothers after their wrongdoing?

options.text: He demands that they be worshipped
He offers pardon rather than reproach
He denies that forgiveness has any value
He asks them to abandon belief in Allah

questions.explanation: Yusuf's response in this verse is an example of mercy and pardon after being wronged.

questions.question: What honor is announced to Maryam in the Quran?

options.text: She became an object of worship
She gained independent power over creation
Allah chose and purified her
She no longer needed to worship Allah

questions.explanation: The angels announce Maryam's selection and purification by Allah.

questions.question: What does Sulayman ask Allah to help him do?

options.text: Use blessings to look down on everyone
Become independent of Allah's mercy
Ignore the blessings given to his parents
Be grateful and perform pleasing good deeds

questions.explanation: Sulayman's prayer joins gratitude for blessings with righteous action and hope in Allah's mercy.

questions.question: How were Musa and Harun told to address Pharaoh?

options.text: With gentle speech
With false promises
With worship directed to him
With praise of his oppression

questions.explanation: Even when confronting Pharaoh's wrongdoing, they were instructed to speak gently.

questions.question: What does Ibrahim ask for himself and his descendants in this dua?

options.text: Freedom from every responsibility
Steadfastness in prayer
Superiority based only on ancestry
A life without needing Allah

questions.explanation: Ibrahim asks Allah to make him and his descendants people who establish prayer.

questions.question: What does the dua beginning 'Rabbana atina' ask for?

options.text: Worldly success with no concern for the Hereafter
Only other people's possessions
Good in this world, good in the Hereafter and protection from the Fire
Knowledge of the exact time of the Last Day

questions.explanation: This Quranic supplication brings worldly and eternal wellbeing together.

questions.question: How does Surah Al-Qadr describe the value of the Night of Decree?

options.text: Exactly the same as every other night
Important only for worldly trade
A night without any connection to worship
Better than a thousand months

questions.explanation: The verse highlights the extraordinary value of Laylat al-Qadr.

questions.question: What does describing the Quran as guidance imply for a learner?

options.text: Its teachings should help shape belief and conduct
Its message matters only as decoration
Understanding is never useful
Its role ends once a beautiful cover is chosen

questions.explanation: The Quran guides toward what is upright; engagement with it includes responding to its guidance.

questions.question: What does the Quran identify as a purpose of sending down the blessed Book?

options.text: Collecting its pages without engaging with them
Reflecting on its verses and taking lessons
Using verses only to win attention
Avoiding thought about their meaning

questions.explanation: This verse explicitly encourages reflection and learning from revelation.

questions.question: What approach to recitation does the command to recite with measured care support?

options.text: Speed regardless of clarity
Skipping words to finish faster
Clear, deliberate recitation
Treating correct wording as unimportant

questions.explanation: Measured recitation values care and clarity rather than rushing through the text.

questions.question: What encouragement is given to someone sincerely struggling to recite the Quran?

options.text: They should stop because only fluent readers matter
Difficulty means their effort is worthless
They should deliberately preserve mistakes
Their effort and difficulty are recognized with reward

questions.explanation: The hadith honors the struggling reciter. It encourages perseverance while learning, not keeping avoidable errors.

questions.question: Why does Quran memorization need regular review?

options.text: Memorized passages can be forgotten without attention
One reading guarantees permanent recall
Revision is only for new converts
Review makes correct memorization less reliable

questions.explanation: The Prophet urged maintaining one's connection with the Quran because memorization can slip away.

questions.question: What does the Quran say about the stories it relates?

options.text: They are only entertainment without guidance
They contain lessons for people of understanding
They require inventing details not mentioned
They replace every command about daily conduct

questions.explanation: Quranic stories offer guidance and lessons rather than merely interesting events.

questions.question: Which inconsistency does the Quran strongly criticize?

options.text: Trying to correct a mistake
Learning before teaching
Saying what one does not do
Admitting a lack of knowledge

questions.explanation: These verses warn against a gap between claims and conduct.

questions.question: Why would quoting only 'do not approach prayer' from this verse be misleading?

options.text: It proves all prayer is forbidden
It shows that the full verse has no meaning
It means any shortened quote is always accurate
It removes the condition about intoxication from the statement

questions.explanation: The phrase is followed by a condition. Reading the full verse prevents a false conclusion about prayer.

questions.question: What attitude helps when a passage is difficult to understand?

options.text: Read in light of clear guidance and seek sound explanation
Build a dramatic claim from an uncertain reading
Assume one's first guess is always final
Ignore all clearer teachings

questions.explanation: The verse identifies clear passages as the Book's foundation and warns against pursuing ambiguity to cause confusion.

questions.question: Who is the Quran described as guidance for in the verse about Ramadan?

options.text: Only one profession
Humanity
Only one economic class
Only people from one modern country

questions.explanation: The verse describes the Quran as guidance for people, not a privilege restricted to a social group.

questions.question: What shared concern connects the warnings against spying and backbiting?

options.text: Making gossip more entertaining
Helping rumors travel faster
Protecting people's privacy and honor
Giving everyone access to private faults

questions.explanation: These commands protect relationships from intrusive and harmful behavior.

questions.question: What purpose is mentioned for humanity being made into peoples and tribes?

options.text: Proving one race is always superior
Removing the need for justice
Making wealth the only source of honor
Knowing one another

questions.explanation: The verse connects human diversity with knowing one another and honor with taqwa.

questions.question: Which combination of qualities does the Quran praise?

options.text: Controlling anger and pardoning people
Suppressing every feeling and seeking revenge
Boasting and humiliating others
Refusing all reconciliation

questions.explanation: The verse presents restraint and forgiveness among the qualities of those who do good.

questions.question: What assumption do these verses correct about prosperity and hardship?

options.text: That people can be tested in their lives
That wealth automatically means honor and limited provision means disgrace
That provision can vary between people
That people should reflect on their response to blessings

questions.explanation: The Quran rejects simplistic judgments of a person's standing based on their material circumstances.

questions.question: What response does the Quran invite from people burdened by past sins?

options.text: Decide that change is impossible
Treat repentance as reserved for people with perfect pasts
Return with hope in Allah's mercy
Assume wrongdoing can never matter

questions.explanation: The call not to despair is an invitation to return to Allah, not a reason to keep doing wrong.

questions.question: Which two responsibilities are joined in this Quranic instruction?

options.text: Seeking fame and displaying wealth
Hiding property and favoring friends
Keeping secrets only when paid
Returning trusts and judging fairly

questions.explanation: The verse joins fulfilling trusts with justice in judgment.

questions.question: What must not be allowed to distort justice?

options.text: Hatred or dislike of a people
Reliable evidence
Honest testimony
A fair hearing

questions.explanation: The Quran requires justice even when we strongly dislike someone.

questions.question: What does the range of people named for kindness show?

options.text: Only relatives deserve care
Good treatment extends beyond one's closest family
Neighbors matter only when wealthy
Strangers can never have a claim to consideration

questions.explanation: The verse includes parents, relatives, vulnerable people, neighbors, companions and travelers among those deserving good treatment.

questions.question: How does the Quran describe balanced spending?

options.text: Spending everything to impress people
Refusing every reasonable need
Avoiding both wastefulness and stinginess
Treating the largest expense as always best

questions.explanation: The verse praises a balanced course between extravagance and miserliness.

questions.question: What principle does the Quran give about claims made without knowledge?

options.text: Confidence alone makes a statement true
Many repetitions turn a rumor into evidence
An attractive design guarantees accuracy
Do not follow or assert what you have no knowledge of

questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes responsibility for what we hear, see and take to heart.

questions.question: A social post cuts a verse at a point that reverses its meaning. What should you do?

options.text: Read the full passage before drawing or sharing a conclusion
Share it because the fragment contains Quranic words
Assume the missing words cannot matter
Choose the interpretation with the most reactions

questions.explanation: A genuine fragment can still be presented misleadingly when essential wording is omitted.

questions.question: You have memorized several surahs and are adding new ones. Which plan best preserves what you know?

options.text: Stop reviewing every completed surah
Include regular revision alongside new learning
Assume one correct recitation makes forgetting impossible
Replace revision with counting how many pages you own

questions.explanation: Regular review helps keep earlier memorization secure while learning continues.

questions.question: A learner feels ashamed because reciting still takes effort. Which reminder fits the hadith?

options.text: Only naturally fluent readers have any value
Difficulty proves they should never open the Quran
Sincere effort in difficulty is rewarded, so continue learning
They should avoid correction to protect their pride

questions.explanation: The hadith supports perseverance and recognizes the struggling learner's effort.

questions.question: Your reading target is making you skip words and rush. What should take priority?

options.text: Finishing the target even with missing words
Competing with a faster reader
Treating clarity as an obstacle
Careful recitation rather than the page count

questions.explanation: A reading target should support measured recitation rather than undermine it.

questions.question: You know a surah's sound but have not explored its message. Which step adds reflection?

options.text: Study a reliable explanation and consider its lessons
Assume knowing the sound removes any need to understand
Invent a meaning based only on how it feels
Treat the message as unrelated to your life

questions.explanation: Sound understanding helps reflection; the Quran itself calls people to ponder its verses.

questions.question: An image claims a sentence is a Quran verse but gives no reference. What should you do before calling it Quran?

options.text: Trust it because the calligraphy is beautiful
Check the wording against a reliable Quran text
Assume a large following proves it is a verse
Invent a surah number for it

questions.explanation: Careful verification applies the principle of not asserting what one does not know.

questions.question: After studying Al-Asr, a group wants one practical habit. Which fits its message?

options.text: Treat time as useful only for earning praise
Ignore good deeds because belief alone is mentioned
Encourage one another toward truth and patience
Make public status the group's main purpose

questions.explanation: The surah joins faith and action with mutual encouragement in truth and patience.

questions.question: A family wants a Quranic example of pardon after wrongdoing. Which passage is directly relevant?

options.text: Pharaoh's claim to authority
The account of building an ark
A passage listing categories of inheritance
Yusuf's response of pardon to his brothers

questions.explanation: Yusuf's words in this verse provide a clear example of forgiveness after personal harm.

questions.question: After receiving a blessing, which response follows Sulayman's prayer?

options.text: Ask Allah for gratitude and help to do good
Assume blessings prove you need no guidance
Use the blessing to belittle others
Forget those whose care helped you

questions.explanation: Sulayman's dua connects appreciation of blessings with righteous action.

questions.question: You are correcting a serious mistake. What lesson can be drawn from Musa and Harun being sent to Pharaoh?

options.text: Gentleness requires calling wrongdoing good
Truth can be conveyed with gentle speech
A harsh tone always proves sincerity
Correction requires humiliating the listener

questions.explanation: Gentle speech and a clear stance against wrongdoing can coexist.

questions.question: You want to make a Quranic dua for your family's worship. Which request follows Ibrahim's example?

options.text: Ask that family status replace every duty
Ask to be excused from caring about worship
Ask Allah to make you and your descendants steadfast in prayer
Ask only to appear religious in public

questions.explanation: Ibrahim's prayer includes both his own worship and that of his descendants.

questions.question: Which request follows the balance of 'Rabbana atina'?

options.text: Ask for wealth while dismissing the Hereafter
Ask only to defeat friends in competition
Ask to gain benefits through any means
Ask for good in this life and the Hereafter

questions.explanation: This dua teaches concern for both worldly wellbeing and the eternal future.

questions.question: You recite the request for the straight path in Al-Fatihah. Which attitude gives it practical meaning?

options.text: Seek guidance sincerely when making choices
Assume every personal desire is already correct
Treat guidance as unnecessary outside prayer
Refuse all opportunities to learn

questions.explanation: Requesting guidance should be accompanied by openness to what is right.

questions.question: While reflecting on An-Nas, you want to respond to a temptation toward wrongdoing. Which action fits the surah?

options.text: Treat every harmful suggestion as a command to obey
Seek refuge in Allah from harmful whispering
Assume protection comes from popularity
Stop seeking Allah's help because thoughts can occur

questions.explanation: An-Nas directs a person to Allah for refuge from the whisperer's evil.

questions.question: Someone claims outward religious display excuses refusing every small kindness. How does Al-Maun challenge this?

options.text: It says care for others has no connection with conduct
It praises humiliating those in need
It criticizes showing off and withholding small help
It makes public praise the aim of prayer

questions.explanation: The surah warns against an outward display disconnected from sincerity and concern for others.

questions.question: After a loss, which Quranic reminder fits 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi rajiun'?

options.text: A believer is guaranteed never to lose anything
Grief makes every act of worship worthless
Loss means Allah no longer knows our situation
We belong to Allah and will return to Him

questions.explanation: The verse gives a reminder of belonging to Allah and returning to Him during hardship.

questions.question: You are evaluating work by members of a group you dislike. Which approach applies this verse?

options.text: Use fair criteria rather than letting dislike lower their marks
Give lower marks purely because of their group
Ignore evidence that favors them
Make dislike the main scoring rule

questions.explanation: The Quran's requirement of justice applies even when personal feelings pull the other way.

questions.question: You manage money entrusted for a group project. Which choice reflects the verse about trusts?

options.text: Use some privately and assume nobody will notice
Keep accurate records and use it for its agreed purpose
Treat access to the funds as personal ownership
Give yourself an unagreed payment in secret

questions.explanation: Fulfilling a trust includes respecting the rights attached to what has been entrusted.

questions.question: You are making a budget that must cover needs and allow generosity. Which choice reflects Quranic balance?

options.text: Spend everything to maintain an impressive image
Refuse essential expenses solely to hoard money
Avoid showy waste while meeting reasonable needs
Decide that any spending is a moral failure

questions.explanation: Balanced spending avoids both extravagance and harmful tightfistedness.

questions.question: A traveler in your community needs reasonable assistance. What does this verse suggest?

options.text: Dismiss them because they are not family
Make their difficulty a public joke
Assume only wealthy visitors deserve respect
Offer considerate help within your ability

questions.explanation: The Quran includes travelers among those toward whom good treatment is directed.
